jobs.title: Staff Environmental Scientist 1
jobs.description:
Find your path and enjoy the journey at Haley & Aldrich. With us, you’ll tackle clients’ most meaningful challenges in the built and natural environments – and, in turn, build stronger communities. You’ll work with teams of passionate colleagues, driven by a commitment to technical excellence and continuous learning.

As a company, we aim to build a world where communities go beyond resilience, embracing change as an opportunity to enhance safety, well-being, and quality of life. Join us to accelerate this vision and your professional development.

We are looking to add new talent to our growing team! We are currently seeking a Staff Environmental Scientist 1, Stormwater to work in a technical support role with highly skilled professionals on diverse project teams in a dynamic environment. This is an excellent opportunity to join a growing group and company and get involved in a variety of projects for a diverse range of clients.

This position offers a recent graduate the opportunity to support stormwater quality management and environmental compliance projects. During the stormwater season, generally October through April, the selected candidate will work primarily in the field at project sites in Ventura/Los Angeles Counties. Responsibilities will include stormwater sampling, compliance inspections, coordination with contractors and laboratories, implementation of standard operating procedures, data management, and technical reporting. Rain-event response will require early-morning starts and on-call availability, including some weekends and potentially holidays. Outside the stormwater season, the position will generally be divided between other field assignments and office-based data analysis and reporting. Due to site-specific permit requirements, the selected candidate must be able to report to the designated primary project site within one hour when required. Relocation assistance is available, if needed. This is a full-time position in the Los Angeles/Ventura County Area assigned virtually to our Costa Mesa, CA office.

Duties/Responsibilities

 In this position, you will: 




 Conduct field investigations and assessments of soil, groundwater, surface water, etc. using approved industry standard procedures.  Conduct basic construction observation, including quality control documentation and field testing tasks.  Conduct or oversee remedial system O&M and field pilot study demonstrations.  Prepare and maintain accurate and detailed documentation of activities both in the field and during data evaluation.  Apply academic training and use computer software to perform calculations and evaluation of information.  Support project environmental data reduction and summarization.  Support project feasibility study, remedial design, cost estimating, and permitting tasks.  Assist with AutoCAD, Civil 3D, and GIS tasks.  Draft technical sections of project communications and reports.  Assist with the development of technical scopes of work and cost estimating for proposal efforts on small- to medium-sized project opportunities.  Perform all work in accordance with company and client health and safety protocols.  Demonstrate the company’s foundational safety behaviors.  Support site-specific environmental compliance activities related to stormwater quality management, construction and post-construction best management practices, NPDES permitting, and California stormwater requirements.  Conduct stormwater sampling, site inspections, and field monitoring activities in accordance with applicable permits, project plans, and standard operating procedures.  Coordinate field activities with project team members, contractors, laboratories, and other project stakeholders.  Assist with permit reviews and the evaluation of applicable local, regional, state, and federal stormwater requirements.  Support stormwater data validation, analysis, visualization, and preparation of compliance reports and other technical deliverables.  Support field programs involving stormwater quality management, contaminated-site investigation and management, and environmental protection-related construction, maintenance, and monitoring. 


Skills/Experience

Minimum Skills and Requirements: 


 Bachelor’s degree in Environmental Science, Water Resources Engineering, Geology, Civil Engineering, or related field.  0 to 2 years of related field experience.  Proficient technical writing, verbal communication, reasoning, and time management skills.  Able to work independently or with minimal direction in performing tasks and assignments under the direction of senior staff.  Desire to learn and grow in your profession, demonstrate a positive attitude, strong work ethic, resourcefulness, flexibility, and ownership.  Familiar with environmental analytical testing and data reduction techniques for soil, water, and air.  Able to meet the physical requirements of the position: lift 50 lbs., traverse unstable/sloping sites and landscapes, work outside in a range of weather conditions, and have the stamina for moderate physical activity for the majority of field working hours.  Able to travel to work locations that may require overnight stays.  Able to work primarily in the field during the stormwater season, generally October through April, including early-morning starts and on-call response during rain events, weekends, and holidays when required.  Able to report to the designated primary project site in Los Angeles/Ventura County area within one hour due to site-specific stormwater permit requirements.  Able to pass client-specific background screenings and obtain required site access badges.  Able to handle large sample volumes and safely operate or ride in field vehicles, including four-wheel-drive vehicles when necessary.  Must have reliable transportation or be able to rent a vehicle for site access; primary project sites are not accessible by public transportation. 


Preferred Skills


 Master’s degree in Environmental Science,

jobs.title: Environmental Specialist
jobs.description:
General Summary

The Environmental Specialist will implement and maintain company protocols adhering to applicable environmental regulations and standards. They will coordinate and work closely with Environmental Health and Safety (EHS), Manufacturing, Plant Engineering, and the Facilities teams to execute environmental compliance tasks and provide technical guidance to stakeholders.

Essential Duties And Responsibilities

Reasonable accommodation may be made to enable qualified individuals to perform the essential functions.

Exercise a high level of professionalism and confidentiality when working with staff, projects, and proprietary information.Operate and maintain measuring equipment to maintain air, land, and water environmental compliance.Manage of material, soil, and water samples to facilitate hazard determination and proper waste classification.Assist in the coordination and use of an Environmental Management System (EMS).Assist in the coordination of the Woodland Pollution Prevention Team.Lead and facilitate Pollution Prevention initiatives.Support Management and all business partners in Environmental compliance task execution.Function as a Clark Pacific (CP) Environmental champion.Participate in Environmental Leadership Councils as directed by Management.Perform Environmental audits and inspections as directed by Management.Execute action items as directed by Management.Verify sustainable completion of Environmental action items as directed by Management.Other duties as assigned.

Key Interfaces

Internal

Environmental ManagerPollution Prevention TeamsManufacturing team membersFacilities DepartmentPlant EngineersDirector of Environmental, Health & Safety

External

Local CUPAYolo County Department of Environmental Health Drinking WaterEnvironmental Consultants

Key Metrics and Deliverables

100% on time Environmental sampling and submittals of media.100% on time completion of Management data submittals and reports.Monitor and measure key performance thresholds as assigned.Report into Management key performance measurements.Immediately report identified deficiencies to Management.

Skills And Abilities

Ability to read and understand technical plans and maps (SWPPP, P&IDs, CUPA, etc.).Willingness to learn how to interpret analytical Lab reports and act upon such information.Ability to appropriately collect air, soil, water, or material samples, containerize and preserve for shipment to Lab for analysis.Ability to complete COCs, technical forms and sample labels.Ability to perform environmental audits, develop corrective actions, and track until closure.Above-average communication skills, both written and verbal, as well as the ability to effectively listen and engage with all levels of the organization.Builds strong relationships; engages and motivates teams representing diverse backgrounds and viewpoints; exceptionally collaborative.Ability to maintain attentiveness to detail and accuracy throughout involvement in multiple projects without losing sight of goals and deadlines.Excellent organization skills.Problem solving skills that aim to remedy and prevent reoccurrence.Comfortable escalating issues while maintaining positive relationships with team members and other organizations.Passionate about Clark Pacific’s vision and mission; able to promote, demonstrate, and communicate the mission, values and core competencies of Clark Pacific to others.Ability to read maps, plans and technical drawings.Able to exercise appropriate discretion when handling confidential and/or sensitive information.Display willingness and interest in stepping up into greater leadership role if the situation requires or the opportunity presents itself.Able to learn and use Microsoft Office Suite programs.

Work Environment

General office environment will be experienced.There will be routine exposure to manufacturing environments which may present hazards such as noise, electricity, chemicals, heavy equipment, and other automated and manual machinery.There will be routine exposure to outside weather conditions, including extreme cold and extreme heat, wet and/or humid environments.

Physical Demands

Frequent: Sitting at desk, utilizing equipment and instruments, computers and phones, standing and walkingPeriodic: Repetitive foot, leg, hand, arm, shoulder, and torso movements. Climbing stairs and ladders.Material handling may be required up to 40 lbs.Occasional Business travel, 5%.Bending squatting, stooping, reaching, pushing, pulling, and lifting.

Experience And Education

High School Diploma or GED required.Heavy manufacturing and/or construction experience is required.Experience in environmental affairs compliance management is strongly preferred.Environmental compliance training and/or education is preferred.

Clark Pacific is an Equal Opportunity Employer
Qualifications
Ability to read and understand technical plans and maps (SWPPP, P&IDs, CUPA, etc.)
Willingness to learn how to interpret analytical Lab reports and act upon such information
Ability to appropriately collect air, soil, water, or material samples, containerize and preserve for shipment to Lab for analysis
Ability to complete COCs, technical forms and sample labels
Above-average communication skills, both written and verbal, as well as the ability to effectively listen and engage with all levels of the organization
Builds strong relationships; engages and motivates teams representing diverse backgrounds and viewpoints; exceptionally collaborative
Ability to maintain attentiveness to detail and accuracy throughout involvement in multiple projects without losing sight of goals and deadlines
Excellent organization skills
Problem solving skills that aim to remedy and prevent reoccurrence
Comfortable escalating issues while maintaining positive relationships with team members and other organizations
Passionate about Clark Pacific’s vision and mission; able to promote, demonstrate, and communicate the mission, values and core competencie
